name: Alchemy Account Kit
description: Alchemy's vertically integrated ERC-4337 stack: smart account (Light Account), bundler, and paymaster in a single provider. The single-vendor AA alternative to the Pimlico + ZeroDev combination. Preferred when an app is already fully invested in the Alchemy infrastructure stack.

ecosystem_fit.notes: Alchemy's primary focus chain for Account Kit. Tight integration with Alchemy RPC and webhooks on Base.
Production AA stack for Ethereum mainnet.
Used as the gasless layer in Farcaster miniapps when the app is already on the Alchemy stack.

common_pairings.context: Account Kit is designed to pair with Alchemy RPC. Single-vendor: Alchemy for RPC + Alchemy for AA. Reduces integration surface when already on Alchemy.
Privy for embedded wallet creation; Alchemy Account Kit for gas sponsorship and smart account features.

trust_evidence.description: Alchemy is one of the top two EVM infrastructure providers. Account Kit is their supported AA product with production usage.
Comprehensive documentation for Account Kit, Light Account, and gas policy management.

scale_guidance.hackathon: Skip — Pimlico has simpler setup for hackathon demos.
scale_guidance.mvp: Valid choice when already on Alchemy RPC. Reduces vendor count.
scale_guidance.production: Preferred over Pimlico only if single-vendor Alchemy stack is a deliberate architectural choice. Compare gas policy flexibility before committing.

alternatives.when_to_prefer: Default AA choice. More flexible: works with any RPC provider, not just Alchemy. Stronger community documentation.
When session keys, plugin system, or Kernel smart account features are required beyond bundler/paymaster.

anti_patterns: Adopting Account Kit just to have a single vendor — the integration complexity of mixing Account Kit with non-Alchemy RPC negates the single-vendor benefit.
Using Account Kit for Solana — ERC-4337 is EVM-only.

sdk_migration.notes: @alchemy/aa-* packages (aa-core, aa-alchemy, aa-ethers) were rebranded to @account-kit/* in mid-2024. The old packages last published August 2024 (v3.19.0) and receive no updates. @account-kit/core is actively maintained. Migration requires code changes beyond a package rename — the API surface changed between aa-sdk v3 and account-kit v4.
